key_insight: A multimodal machine-learning framework combined clinical, imaging, and biofluid data to identify biomarkers and create a digital dashboard for tracking childhood-onset neurodegenerative disease progression.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help stratify patients, monitor disease more objectively, and improve readiness for future therapeutic trials in ultra-rare pediatric neurological disorders.
method: Natural history study of 310 PLAN patients plus longitudinal neuroimaging and multiomic biomarker collection
Developed a disease-specific clinical scale (CoPLAN-DRS) and integrated data with machine learning
Built a Digital Disease Dashboard to visualize disease severity in a clinically intuitive format
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong correlations between disease measures and age, including CoPLAN-DRS (rho=0.69) and MRI quantitative susceptibility mapping (rho=0.96), plus biomarker associations such as neurofilament light (rho=-0.74).
watch_item: Findings are from a rare-disease cohort and require external validation before the dashboard or biomarker set can be generalized or used in routine care.
paper_title: A Multimodal Multiomics Machine Learning (MMM) approach for biomarker discovery and acceleration of clinical trial readiness for childhood-onset neurological disorders
